(Source: Lynes, 1999)

cr_data.provenance: An American Place, New York, 1936. The Downtown Gallery, New York, about 1936–1937; Arthur Milliken, Simsbury, Conn., 1937–1965; Yale University Art Gallery, New Haven, Conn., 1965. (Source: Yale University Art Gallery, 2025)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Infor. from O'Keeffe. Sold by Mrs. Halpert." Backing inscription dates 1937. Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks date 1936. Dated 1936 on basis of inclusion in 1937 exhibition and Stieglitz–O'Keeffe correspondence. The name in the title refers to Robert Johnson, a friend of the artist. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.notes: Source of title: Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks, 1937 New York (An American Place–O'Keeffe) exhibition checklist.
titles.title: Bob's Steer Head

credit_line: Yale University Art Gallery, Gift of Arthur Milliken, B.A. 1926
description: A large steer's head with wide horns occupies the center of the canvas. The head is mounted on a brown wall, and a piece of animal hide with hair is draped over the top of it.
imageCaption: Image courtesy of a scanned transparency made for Georgia O'Keeffe: Catalogue Raisonné. This image has not been color proofed and may differ from the original. It will be replaced when newer photography becomes available.
